title: Imaging Integrin Tension and Cellular Force at Submicron Resolution with an Integrative Tension Sensor
protocol: Deprotect the thiol modifier on the upper strand DNA using TCEP solution.
Conjugate RGD peptide to the SH-ssDNA-quencher using PBS, sulfo-SMCC, and RGD peptide.
Dissolve 14.3 mg of TCEP-HCl in 300 µL of water.
Adjust the pH of the TCEP solution to ~7.2–7.4 with 1 M NaOH solution, using pH test papers.
Add pure water to make a final volume of 0.5 mL.
Add 100 µL of 0.5 M EDTA solution and 400 µL of water to the TCEP solution.
Add 10 µL of the TCEP+EDTA solution to 20 µL of 1 mM thiol-DNA-BHQ2 in PBS.
Let the solution react for 30 min at room temperature.
Add 200 µL of pure water to the tube containing 2 mg of sulfo-SMCC.
Smash the sulfo-SMCC solid with a pipette tip and vigorously pipette to dissolve it in the water.
Add 40 µL of dissolved sulfo-SMCC to the 100 µL RGD-NH₂ solution.
Incubate the mixture for 20 min at room temperature.
Mix the solutions prepared in steps 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 and incubate the mixture for 1 h at room temperature.
Move the solution to a refrigerator set at 4 °C and let it further react overnight.
Chill 10 mL of 100% ethanol in a 15 mL conical tube in a -20 °C freezer for at least 30 min.
Mix a 3 M NaCl solution, a DNA solution, and chilled ethanol at a volume ratio of 1:10:25.
Keep the mixed liquid in a -20 °C freezer for 30 min or until the DNA is precipitated.
Centrifuge the liquid at 10,000 x g for 30 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add PBS to the DNA pellet.
Measure the DNA concentration using a spectrometer.
Assemble a vertical electrophoresis system.
Prepare a 10% polyacrylamide gel solution by mixing pure water, 40% acrylamide gel, 10x TBE buffer, and APS at specified volumes.
Add TEMED to the gel solution.
Pour the gel solution into the glass chamber of the electrophoresis system.
Insert a single-well comb to create a well on top of the gel.
Wait for 10 min until the gel is crosslinked.
Mix the DNA solution with 100% glycerol at a volume ratio of 1:1.
Remove the comb and load the DNA solution into the gel well.
Run the gel at a voltage of 200 V.
Observe two DNA bands, with the lagging one being the conjugated DNA.
Cut the gel band with the conjugated DNA off.
Dice the cut gel band into small pieces.
Collect diced gel in two 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes with filters.
Add 500 µL of PBS to each tube.
Put the PBS-soaked gel in a dark place at room temperature for 1 day.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,000 x g for 2 min to collect the DNA solution.
Perform another round of ethanol precipitation to collect the DNA.
Mix solutions of RGD-ssDNA-quencher and dye-ssDNA-biotin at a molar ratio of 1.1:1.
Keep the mixture at 4 °C overnight to produce the ITS by DNA hybridization.
Aliquot and store the ITS solution at -20 °C for long-term storage.
Chill biotinylated bovine serum albumin (BSA-biotin), avidin protein, and PBS buffer to around 0 °C on ice.
Load 200 µL of 0.1 mg/mL BSA-biotin in PBS onto the well of a glass-bottomed Petri dish.
Incubate it for 30 min at 4 °C.
Suck out the solution from the well using a pipette.
Add 200 µL of PBS back to the well to wash the surface.
Repeat this step 3 times.
Incubate 200 µL of 50 µg/mL avidin protein in the well for 30 min at 4 °C.
Wash it 3 times with PBS.
Incubate 200 µL of 0.1 µM ITS in the well for 30 min at 4 °C.
Wash the dish with 3 times with PBS.
Leave PBS in the well until the cell plating.
Culture fish keratocytes.
Pluck a piece of fish scale from a fish with a flat-tip tweezer.
Gently press the scale onto the well of a glass-bottomed Petri dish, with the inner side contacting the glass.
Wait for ~30 s for the fish scale to adhere well to the glass surface of the dish.
Add 1 mL of Iscove’s modified Dulbecco’s medium (IMDM) complete medium to fully cover the fish scale.
Keep the Petri dish in a dark and humid box for 6–48 h at room temperature.
Remove the medium from the Petri dish in which the fish scale was cultured.
Wash the well once with cell detaching solution.
Add detaching solution to cover the fish scale.
Incubate for 3 min.
Suck out all cell detaching solution and add IMDM complete medium.
Disperse the keratocytes by gentle pipetting.
Adjust the cell solution density to the desired level (1 x 104–1 x 105/mL).
Plate the cells on the ITS surface.
Incubate the cells at room temperature for 30 min before imaging.
Culture CHO-K1 cells or NIH 3T3 cells to 80%–100% confluence in a Petri dish (or culture flask).
Warm the cell detaching solution and culture medium to 37 °C.
Remove all culture medium in the Petri dish with a pipette.
Wash the cells 1x with cell detaching solution.
Cover the cells with detaching solution and incubate it at 37 °C for 10 min.
Disperse the cells by pipetting.
Collect the cell solution and centrifuge it at 300 x g for 3 min.
Suck out the supernatant and add complete medium or serum-free medium.
Adjust the cell solution density to the desired level (1 x 10^5 – 1 x 10^6/mL).
Plate the cells on the ITS surfaces.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C for 1–2 h before imaging, or 30 min before video recording.
Incubate keratocytes on ITS surfaces for 30 min at room temperature, or incubate CHO-K1 cells or NIH 3T3 cells for 1 h on ITS surfaces in an incubator at 37 °C.
Mount the Petri dish on a fluorescence microscope stage.
Perform cellular force imaging with an exposure time of 1 s using a magnification of 40x or 100x.
Take a video of ITS images with a frame interval of 20 s for keratocytes, or 1–2 min for CHO-K1 cells or NIH 3T3 cells.
Subtract a previous frame of the ITS video from a current frame to compute the ITS signal newly produced in the latest frame interval using MATLAB or another image analysis tool.
Use the newly produced ITS signal to report the cellular force in a quasi-real-time manner.
After step 3.2.2 or step 3.3.6, perform immunostaining to mark the target structural proteins.
Use different dyes to avoid fluorescence crosstalk between integrin tension imaging and cell structural imaging.
Use Cy5 fluorophore for phalloidin staining.
Use Alexa 488 for vinculin staining.
Prepare primary and secondary antibody solutions at a concentration of 2.5 µg/mL.
Prepare phalloidin solution at a concentration of 1.5 units/µL.
Perform multifluorescent channel imaging to acquire an integrin tension map.
Acquire cell structural images using the same imaging setup.
